title: PortCVE listener lockfile v1
description: A deterministic, normalized, privacy-reduced baseline of local endpoints. Volatile process data and raw private process/container evidence are not stored, but normalized owner identities, including image-set hashes, can still fingerprint installed or running software.

created_by.description: The PortCVE tool and version that wrote the lockfile.

includes_udp.description: Whether UDP binds are part of this baseline and must be included in later diff/check collection.

allow_weak_owner.description: Explicit policy opt-in permitting name_only owner identities to support check decisions. Missing means false. unknown owner identities remain incomplete, and objective ownership evidence remains partial when any name_only identity is present.

listeners.description: Normalized listener records. PortCVE also enforces a 16 MiB total lockfile input limit before deserialization.

selector.description: The port/protocol selector captured with the baseline. Null selector members are omitted. Schema v1 does not accept process or scope selectors.

containers.description: Docker publication evidence used for this baseline: complete when the local Engine answered, partial after access denial, timeout, invalid response, or API failure, or not_collected when the optional local Docker pipe was absent.

owner_identity.description: Normalized owner identity, for example a binary SHA-256, deterministic Docker image-set SHA-256, service, kernel, process-name, or unknown identity. Container IDs, names, and raw image references are never stored here.

owner_identity_strength.description: container_image means owner_identity is the hash of the sorted distinct Docker image-ID set correlated to this host endpoint, not direct proof of guest-process ownership.

host_policy.description: A static Windows Firewall policy assessment, not a packet-path or external-reachability result.
